title: Why Is There a Pit Under Subway Tracks?
description:
In many London Underground stations, if you look down from the platform, the space between the rails is not flat. There is a deep trench, almost a meter deep, running under the track. It is there for drainage and for workers. But it has another, darker job. It has saved the lives of people who fell, or jumped, in front of a train. Today, eleven parts of a subway, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:16 1. The pit under the track
2:40 2. The covered rail
4:01 3. The fourth rail
5:17 4. The arm that stops trains
6:33 5. The glass wall
7:48 6. The bumpy tiles
9:08 7. The rubber tyres
10:35 8. The station on a hill
11:49 9. The gap
13:05 10. The metal escalator
14:34 11. The vent shaft
15:48 The verdict

Sources:
- Anti-suicide (drainage) pits and mortality: T.J. Coats, D.P. Walter, "Effect of station design on death in the London Underground: observational study", BMJ 319 (1999) 957 https://www.bmj.com/content/319/7215/957
- London Underground history (1863) and four-rail electrification: Wikipedia, "London Underground" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Underground and "Railway electrification in Great Britain" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_rail
- New York City Subway third rail (625 V DC): Wikipedia, "Third rail" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_rail
- Train stops and trip cocks: Wikipedia, "Train stop" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_stop
- Platform screen doors and Park Pobedy (1961): Wikipedia, "Platform screen doors" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_screen_doors and "Park Pobedy (Saint Petersburg Metro)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Pobedy_(Saint_Petersburg_Metro)
- Tactile paving (Seiichi Miyake, Okayama 1967): Wikipedia, "Tactile paving" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tactile_paving
- Rubber-tyred metro (Paris line 11, 1956): Wikipedia, "Rubber-tyred metro" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubber-tyred_metro
- Humped stations on the Central and Victoria lines: Wikipedia, "Central line (London Underground)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_line_(London_Underground) and "Victoria line" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_line
- Mind the gap and Oswald Laurence: BBC News (2013), "Widow's 'Mind the Gap' request granted" https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-21402213
- King's Cross fire (1987, 31 deaths) and the trench effect: Wikipedia, "King's Cross fire" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King%27s_Cross_fire
- Piston effect and tunnel ventilation: Wikipedia, "Piston effect" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piston_effect
